key_insight: Neural Fourier Surrogates (NFS) provide a classical model that matches the finite Fourier-series support of data-reuploading quantum neural networks, making them a more direct baseline for judging quantum performance.
engineering_relevance: NFS offers a practical benchmarking tool for quantum machine learning by separating gains due to Fourier feature structure from gains due to genuine quantum effects.
method: Stochastic classical neural architecture that learns coefficients over the same finite Fourier support as QNNs.
Inspired by Neural Quantum States and Random Fourier Features.
Compared against tabular benchmarks, Random Fourier Features, and data-reuploading QNNs; Fourier spectra also analyzed on synthetic data.
evidence_signal: On a selection of tabular benchmark datasets, NFS was broadly competitive with established classical baselines and achieved performance comparable to data-reuploading QNNs, with synthetic-data analysis showing similar learned Fourier spectra.
watch_item: As a stochastic surrogate, NFS still depends on Fourier support choices and training stability, so benchmark conclusions may be sensitive to architecture and optimization details.
paper_title: Neural Fourier Surrogates for Data Reuploading Quantum Neural Networks
